# Neurons: the cells of nervous tissue

<!-- STEP id="neuron" -->
## Nerve cells
The cells of nervous tissue are called **neurons**, or nerve cells. They are specialised to receive, process and transmit (pass on) messages.

<!-- STEP id="parts" -->
## Three main parts
Each neuron has three main parts:

- the **cell body**, which contains the nucleus and controls the activities of the cell,
- the **dendrites**, short branches that receive signals from other neurons,
- the **axon**, a long fibre that carries messages away from the cell body.

<!-- STEP id="terminals" -->
## Passing the message on
The axon ends in **axon terminals**. The axon terminals transmit the message to other cells, such as another neuron or a muscle.

<!-- STEP id="path" -->
## One way through the cell
A message enters at the dendrites, passes the cell body and travels along the axon to its terminals. Like the wire from a switch to a lamp, a long axon links two places that are far apart, but unlike a wire, a neuron is a living cell.

**A neuron receives a message at its dendrites and passes it on from its axon terminals.**
